mainTopic: Who accepts קידושין, a גט, and מאמר for a נערה: the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, its sources, and how the study hall decided it
overview: This amud asks who may accept קידושין, a גט, and מאמר for a נערה. A ברייתא says a נערה can accept מאמר herself. This forces the גמרא to restate רבי יוחנן's reason: קידושין needs consent, so only the father accepts it, while a גט works against her will, so either she or her father may accept it. מאמר seems to need consent too. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי, who learns מאמר from ביאה of a יבמה, while חכמים learn it from regular קידושין. The ending of the ברייתא, 'unlike קידושין', supports רבי יוחנן. ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and in the end the special bond of a יבמה (זקוקה ועומדת) explains מאמר and clears רבי יוחנן as well. Our משנה also seems to refute ריש לקיש. The גמרא concludes that the whole משנה follows רבי שמעון, who agrees with רבי יהודה on agency. A story then reports that the study hall sided with רבי יוחנן, though ריש לקיש cried out a פסוק, and the report is confirmed as reliable and quoted from an unspecified רבי אבין. The amud ends as רבא begins a new question to רב נחמן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: a נערה can accept מאמר herself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: a קטנה can receive מאמר only with her father's consent, but a נערה can receive it with her own consent or her father's. This challenges the earlier explanation of רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: A minor girl who was widowed after betrothal: the brother may do מאמר with her only with her father's consent. But a young woman: either with her own consent or with her father's consent (which is not so with regular betrothal).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about מאמר, the special יבום-betrothal a brother gives his late brother's widow. The ברייתא's last line is used to attack an earlier explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a נערה can accept מאמר on her own consent. Yet מאמר also takes her out of her father's control, just like קידושין does. So the earlier reason, that a girl cannot accept something that removes her from her father, seems wrong. That is why the next step restates the explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A young woman in the six months after she turns twelve, still under her father's authority
Betrothal of a יבמה by the brother-in-law, using money or a document
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up a קטנה and a נערה. A קטנה needs her father for מאמר. A נערה can accept מאמר herself, and that is exactly what makes this a challenge.

phrases.english: A minor girl [widowed] from betrothal —
one may not perform מאמר with her
except with her father's consent.
And the young woman —

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִדַּעַת עַצְמָהּ בֵּין מִדַּעַת אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: either with her own consent or with her father's consent,
(which is not so with regular betrothal).
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some leave them out. With regular קידושין, a נערה can't accept it on her own.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְטַנָּה מִן הָאֵירוּסִין אֵין עוֹשִׂים בָּהּ מַאֲמָר אֶלָּא מִדַּעַת אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא begun before this section, which is being used against the earlier explanation of רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation of why a נערה cannot accept her own קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מאמר also takes her out of her father's authority, yet the ברייתא lets a נערה accept it herself

steps.title: Restating רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: consent versus no consent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates the explanation. קידושין needs consent, so only the father accepts it. A גט works against her will, so either she or her father can accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: What is the reason of רבי יוחנן according to the רבנן? Betrothal, which needs consent: her father, and not she. Divorce, which can be against her will: either she or her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old version of the explanation and gives a corrected version of what רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא really said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reason is about consent, not about leaving her father's control. Anything that needs consent depends on the father's consent, so he alone accepts it. A גט can be given even against her will, so her consent doesn't matter, and she can receive it just as well as her father.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a statement)
According to the view of the רבנן

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the working rule. Whether something needs her consent decides who may accept it.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan
according to the Rabbis?
Betrothal, which is with her consent —
her father [accepts it], and not she.
Divorce, which can be against her will —
either she or her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 1 challenged
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason was that a girl cannot accept something that removes her from her father's authority
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason is consent: what needs consent goes through the father, and what works against her will can go through either of them

steps.title: But מאמר also needs her consent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reason. מאמר needs consent like קידושין, yet the ברייתא says either she or her father can accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But מאמר is with her consent, and it teaches: either she or her father!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation with the same ברייתא from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 2, anything that needs consent can only go through the father. But מאמר is a kind of betrothal and needs her consent. Still, the ברייתא lets a נערה accept it herself.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here is (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But מאמר is with her consent,
and it teaches: either she or her father!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the restated explanation in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that anything needing consent goes only through the father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מאמר needs consent, yet the ברייתא lets either she or her father accept it

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי: מאמר works against her will
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about מאמר that works against her will, which is the view of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is talking about מאמר that is against her will, and it follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי, who holds that מאמר works even without her consent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, מאמר is like a גט: it doesn't need her consent. So by the rule of step 2, either she or her father may accept it. Step 2's rule still stands.

phrases.english: There it is talking about מאמר that is against her will,
and it follows Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּמַאֲמָר דִּבְעַל כֻּרְחַהּ וְרַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to one תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מאמר always needs consent, so the ברייתא contradicts the rule
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי, for whom מאמר works against her will, so it fits the rule

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי and חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי holds מאמר without her consent works, and חכמים say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If one does מאמר with his יבמה without her consent, רבי says: he acquired her. And the חכמים say: he did not acquire her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי really holds מאמר works against her will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves the claim in step 4. רבי says the יבם acquires her even without her consent. The חכמים say he does not, so for them מאמר needs her consent.

keyTerms.meaning: His יבמה, his late brother's widow

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: מאמר works even without her consent. חכמים: it needs her consent.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who does מאמר with his יבמה
without her consent,
Rabbi says: he acquired her,
and the Sages say: he did not acquire her.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא הָעוֹשֶׂה מַאֲמָר בִּיבִמְתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4's claim about רבי
steps.raayaObject: That רבי holds מאמר works against her will
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the מחלוקת of רבי and חכמים

steps.title: Asking for רבי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי holds that מאמר works without her consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks for the source behind רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for an explanation, not an attack. The answer will also show why חכמים disagree.

phrases.english: What is Rabbi's reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי's view from step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי's view that מאמר works against her will

steps.title: רבי learns מאמר from ביאה of a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי compares מאמר to ביאה with a יבמה, which works even against her will.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from ביאה with a יבמה. Just as ביאה with a יבמה works against her will, so too here, it works against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי's reason. He compares מאמר to the main act of יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main יבום, done through ביאה, works even without her consent. רבי treats מאמר as part of יבום, so it works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations with a יבמה, the main act of יבום

phrases.english: He learns it from ביאה with a יבמה,
just as ביאה with a יבמה works against her will —
so too here, it works against her will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי learns מאמר from ביאה of a יבמה, which works against her will

steps.title: חכמים learn מאמר from regular קידושין
steps.stepSummary: חכמים compare מאמר to regular קידושין, which needs her consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold: we learn it from betrothal. Just as betrothal is with her consent, so too here, it is with her consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the חכמים's reason, which compares מאמר to a different source than רבי does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מאמר looks like regular קידושין, since it is done with money or a document. So the חכמים say it follows the rules of קידושין and needs her consent. The whole מחלוקת comes down to which act מאמר resembles more.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי compares מאמר to ביאה of a יבמה, so it works without consent. חכמים compare it to קידושין, so it needs consent. The ברייתא that lets a נערה accept מאמר follows רבי.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
we learn it from betrothal,
just as betrothal is with her consent —
so too here, it is with her consent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reason, alongside רבי's in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חכמים learn מאמר from regular קידושין, which needs her consent

steps.title: The root of the argument between רבי and רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns the laws of a יבמה from other laws of a יבמה. רבנן learn the laws of קידושין from regular קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is their argument really about? רבי holds that we should learn laws of a יבמה from other laws of a יבמה. רבנן hold that we should learn laws of קידושין from regular קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the core of the argument from steps 7 and 8 by naming which source each side learns from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מאמר looks like two things at once. It is a step toward יבום, which can happen against her will, and it is also a kind of קידושין, which needs her consent. רבי follows the יבום side, and רבנן follow the קידושין side.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the root of their argument?
A widow who is waiting for יבום with her late husband's brother

phrases.english: About what do they argue?
רבי holds:

phrases.aramaic: מִילֵּי דִיבָמָה מִיבָמָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף.
phrases.english: Matters of a יבמה should be learned from a יבמה.
phrases.notes: Since ביאה with a יבמה works even against her will, רבי says מאמר works that way too.

phrases.english: And רבנן hold:
קידושין should be learned from קידושין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the two reasons given in steps 7 and 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the underlying point of the argument?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each side compares מאמר to a different source: רבי compares it to יבום, and רבנן compare it to regular קידושין.

steps.title: The ברייתא's ending supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that a נערה can accept מאמר herself, 'unlike קידושין.' This shows that in regular קידושין only her father accepts, which is רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense to explain the way רבי יוחנן does, since the end of the ברייתא says: 'which is not so with קידושין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן from the last line of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that for מאמר, either the נערה or her father may accept, and then adds 'unlike קידושין.' So in regular קידושין she cannot accept for herself, and only her father can. That matches what רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: This also makes sense (a support is coming)
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable
as רבי יוחנן explains,
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן said that according to רבנן, only the father accepts קידושין for a נערה.

phrases.english: since the last part teaches:
"which is not so with קידושין."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא and uses its ending as support for רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that only the father can accept קידושין for a נערה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the ברייתא: 'which is not so with קידושין'

steps.title: Is this a refutation of ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן, it seems to disprove ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then shall we say this is a refutation of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the support for רבי יוחנן into a challenge against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that a נערה can accept her own קידושין. The ברייתא says that she can accept מאמר 'unlike קידושין,' which seems to go directly against him.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong challenge that disproves a view

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ?
phrases.english: So shall we say this is a refutation of ריש לקיש?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the support in step 10 means for ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a נערה can accept her own קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that only in מאמר, not in קידושין, can she accept for herself.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who holds that two hands cannot acquire together. So the ברייתא is not the view of רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can answer you: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה's, who says that two hands do not acquire together.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש escapes the challenge by assigning the ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a girl and her father cannot both have the power to receive. So in his view only the father can. The ברייתא's 'unlike' line reflects רבי יהודה, so ריש לקיש's reading of רבנן is not disproved.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hands do not acquire as one, so both father and daughter cannot receive

phrases.english: ריש לקיש can say to you:
Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה's,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֵין שְׁתֵּי יָדַיִם זוֹכוֹת כְּאַחַת.
phrases.english: who says: two hands do not acquire as one.
phrases.notes: In the משנה, רבי יהודה said this about receiving a גט: only the father receives it, not the girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against ריש לקיש in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ברייתא to a different תנא (רבי יהודה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא reflects רבנן and disproves ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, so ריש לקיש's reading of רבנן still stands.

steps.title: Then it should have said 'unlike divorce'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's ruling was about receiving a גט. So if the ברייתא follows him, it should say 'unlike גירושין,' not 'unlike קידושין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי יהודה, why say 'unlike קידושין'? It should have said 'unlike גירושין'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's answer based on the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule of 'two hands' was said about receiving a גט. A ברייתא following him should compare מאמר to divorce, but it compares it to קידושין instead.

phrases.english: If it is רבי יהודה,
why "which is not so with קידושין"?!

phrases.aramaic: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּגֵירוּשִׁין מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: It should have said "which is not so with divorce"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה spoke about divorce, so the ברייתא's mention of קידושין does not fit him.

steps.title: It mentions קידושין only because מאמר is like קידושין
steps.stepSummary: Yes, divorce would have been the more exact choice. But since מאמר looks like קידושין, the ברייתא chose 'unlike קידושין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But since it was teaching about מאמר, which is like קידושין, it also said 'unlike קידושין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the point about wording but explains why the ברייתא phrased it this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real contrast is with divorce. The ברייתא simply used the natural comparison, because מאמר is a kind of betrothal.

keyTerms.meaning: A יבם's betrothal of the יבמה with money or a document

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
since it taught מאמר, which is similar to קידושין,

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא נָמֵי: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּקִידּוּשִׁין.
phrases.english: it also taught: "which is not so with קידושין."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording as a natural association
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word קידושין shows that the ברייתא cannot follow רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really means 'unlike divorce' but says קידושין because מאמר resembles it.

steps.title: Why is מאמר different for רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, why can the girl accept מאמר herself when she cannot receive a גט herself?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה, what is different about מאמר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's distinction. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both מאמר and divorce can happen without her consent. So why would 'two hands do not acquire as one' block her from receiving a גט but not from accepting מאמר?

phrases.english: And according to רבי יהודה, what is different about מאמר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, the גמרא asks how his view makes sense.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה lets a נערה accept מאמר but not receive her own גט

steps.title: She is already bound to the יבם
steps.stepSummary: מאמר is different because the יבמה is already tied to the יבם and waiting for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because she is already bound to him and waiting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is already a bond between the יבמה and the יבם, since she is waiting for him. Because of that existing bond, her own acceptance of the מאמר is enough, even for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Already bound (to the יבם) and waiting

steps.whatToRemember: מאמר is special because the יבמה is already זקוקה to the יבם.

phrases.english: Since she is already bound and standing (waiting for him).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The existing זיקה to the יבם makes her own acceptance of מאמר enough.

steps.title: The same reason clears רבי יוחנן from the start
steps.stepSummary: With the 'already bound' reason, the original challenge against רבי יוחנן from this ברייתא falls away. מאמר is simply different from regular קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, רבי יוחנן also should not have been a difficulty for you from the beginning: מאמר is different, because she is already bound and waiting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the reason from step 16 and uses it to fully defend רבי יוחנן as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that in regular קידושין only the father accepts. The ברייתא lets her accept מאמר herself, which seemed to contradict him. Now we see that מאמר is a special case because of the existing bond, so there was never a real contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this

steps.whatToRemember: The 'already bound' reason explains רבי יהודה and also protects רבי יוחנן: מאמר is a special case, so it says nothing about regular קידושין.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one reason can settle two problems. Because מאמר is unusual, rules about it cannot simply be carried over to ordinary קידושין.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נָמֵי לָא תִּיקְשֵׁי לָךְ מֵעִיקָּרָא:
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן also should not be a difficulty for you from the outset:
phrases.notes: He means the earlier question on רבי יוחנן from this ברייתא, where she accepts מאמר herself.

phrases.english: מאמר is different,
since she is already bound and standing (waiting for him).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 16 to settle the original challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מאמר is a special case because of the existing זיקה, so the ברייתא does not contradict רבי יוחנן about regular קידושין.

steps.title: The משנה seems to refute ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a father betroths his נערה daughter himself or through his agent. This implies she cannot do it herself, which contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: A man can betroth his daughter when she is a נערה, by himself or through his agent. Himself or his agent, yes. Herself or her agent, no. This refutes ריש לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to ריש לקיש and attacks his view using the wording of our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that according to the חכמים a נערה can accept her own קידושין. The משנה lists only the father and the father's agent. The גמרא reads that list as excluding the girl and her agent, so the משנה seems to disagree with ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl between age 12 and 12½, still under her father's authority

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never says outright that the girl cannot accept קידושין herself. The גמרא is learning this from what the משנה leaves out ('him and his agent, yes; her and her agent, no').

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה:
A man betroths his daughter
when she is a נערה, by himself or through his agent.
By himself or his agent, yes,
by herself or her agent, no.
This is a refutation of ריש לקיש!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה, בּוֹ וּבִשְׁלוּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge against רבי יוחנן was resolved, the גמרא now challenges the other side, ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that, according to the חכמים, a נערה can accept her own קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions only the father and his agent, which implies the girl and her agent cannot accept קידושין.

steps.title: ריש לקיש says this משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש can answer that this משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds the girl cannot act for herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can say to you: This משנה too follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself by saying the משנה follows a single תנא, רבי יהודה, and not the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש only claimed that the חכמים let a נערה accept her own קידושין. If the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who says she cannot act for herself, then it does not contradict what ריש לקיש says about the חכמים.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש can say to you:
This משנה too follows רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא (רבי יהודה) whose view differs from the חכמים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה reflects the general הלכה, so it contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה alone, so ריש לקיש's view of the חכמים still stands.

steps.title: A later clause of the same משנה points to a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה can really follow רבי יהודה, since a later clause about betrothing with two dates was attributed to another תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you really place this משנה as רבי יהודה? The later clause teaches: One who says to a woman, 'Be betrothed to me with this date, be betrothed to me with this one.' And we asked: Who is the תנא who taught that 'be betrothed, be betrothed' must be said separately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's answer by pointing to a later clause in the same משנה. This step sets up the problem, and the next step shows which תנא that clause follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man says 'be betrothed' separately for each date, each date is counted on its own and must be worth a פרוטה by itself. Elsewhere the גמרא asked whose view this is. If that clause belongs to a תנא other than רבי יהודה, it is hard to say the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: You establish (place a source as following a certain view)
The later clause of a משנה
Who is the תנא (whose view is this)?

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: But can you really place it as following רבי יהודה?
But the later clause teaches:
One who says to a woman:
'Be betrothed to me with this date,'
'Be betrothed to me with this one'
And we asked: Who is the תנא
who taught 'be betrothed,' 'be betrothed'?
phrases.notes: He means: whose view says each date counts separately only when 'be betrothed' is said for each one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that our משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another clause of the same משנה was already assigned to a specific תנא. The משנה should be one consistent view, so that clause limits who the משנה can follow.

steps.title: רבה: that clause follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבה said the 'be betrothed, be betrothed' clause follows רבי שמעון, who requires the word 'oath' for each person in order to be liable for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: It is רבי שמעון, who says one is not liable separately unless he says 'oath' to each and every one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its challenge by quoting רבה, who identified that later clause as the view of רבי שמעון and not רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that with oaths, saying 'oath' once for several people counts as one act. Saying 'oath' to each person counts as separate acts. The same logic applies to 'be betrothed' said for each date. So that clause follows רבי שמעון, which seems to show the משנה is not רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And רבה said: It is רבי שמעון,
who says: Not unless he says
phrases.notes: This is about someone who falsely swears to several people that he does not have their items.

phrases.english: 'oath' to each and every one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence that drives the challenge of step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That the later clause of the משנה follows רבי שמעון, not רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's identification, based on רבי שמעון's rule about oaths needing to be said to each person separately.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim in step 19 that our משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה assigned the 'be betrothed, be betrothed' clause of the same משנה to רבי שמעון, so the משנה cannot simply be attributed to רבי יהודה

steps.title: Could רבי יהודה agree with רבי שמעון on this one point?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the whole משנה might be רבי יהודה, who agrees with רבי שמעון about separate expressions. It then questions whether רבי יהודה really holds that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the whole משנה is רבי יהודה, and on the matter of saying each item separately he holds like רבי שמעון, does he really hold that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way out for ריש לקיש and immediately questions it. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will check what רבי יהודה actually holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The escape is that two תנאים can agree on one detail, so the whole משנה could still be רבי יהודה. The גמרא rejects this as an easy assumption and asks for evidence. If רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי שמעון on this point, the escape fails.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a possible answer is raised)
The whole of it (the entire משנה)
But does he really hold that?

phrases.english: And if you say the whole משנה is רבי יהודה,
and on specifying each item separately he holds like רבי שמעון,
but does he really hold that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and questions a possible defense against the challenge of steps 20-21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי שמעון about separate expressions.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no basis to assume רבי יהודה holds like רבי שמעון on this point. The גמרא is about to show he may not.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי שמעון on oaths
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four views on when a person brings a separate קרבן for each person in a false oath. רבי יהודה's view is clearly different from רבי שמעון's.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: This is the rule. If he included everyone together, he is liable only once. If he named each one separately, he is liable for each one. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says: If he said 'An oath, I don't have yours, nor yours, nor yours,' he is liable for each one. רבי אליעזר says: If he said 'Not yours, not yours, not yours, and not yours, an oath,' he is liable for each one. רבי שמעון says: He is never liable for each one unless he says the word 'oath' to each person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea from step 22 that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי שמעון. It quotes a ברייתא where they plainly disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, saying 'oath' once at the start is enough to make a separate obligation for each person. רבי שמעון demands the word 'oath' for every single person. So the 'be betrothed, be betrothed' clause, which follows רבי שמעון, cannot also be רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: He included everything in one statement
Liable separately for each one (a קרבן for each)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in all four opinions. The only point that matters here is that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: This is the principle:
If he included them together, he is liable only once,
phrases.notes: This is about someone who falsely swears he isn't holding other people's deposits, and must bring a קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: פָּרַט – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת,
phrases.english: if he specified them, he is liable for each and every one,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: ״שְׁבוּעָה לֹא לָךְ, לֹא לָךְ, לֹא לָךְ״
phrases.english: "An oath: not yours, not yours, not yours"
phrases.notes: "Not yours" means "I don't have your deposit," said to each person in turn.

phrases.english: he is liable for each and every one.
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא לָךְ, לֹא לָךְ, לֹא לָךְ וְלֹא לָךְ שְׁבוּעָה״
phrases.english: "Not yours, not yours, not yours, and not yours, an oath"
he is liable for each and every one.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: He is never liable for each

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר שְׁבוּעָה לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: unless he says "oath" to each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 22 that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי שמעון about separate expressions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows רבי יהודה needs 'oath' only once while רבי שמעון needs it for each person, so they disagree, and the 'be betrothed, be betrothed' clause (רבי שמעון) cannot be רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The whole משנה is רבי שמעון, who agrees with רבי יהודה on agency
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the approach: the whole משנה follows רבי שמעון, and on agency רבי שמעון holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the whole משנה is רבי שמעון, and on the topic of agency he holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that keeps the משנה from contradicting ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of making רבי יהודה agree with רבי שמעון on oaths, it makes רבי שמעון agree with רבי יהודה on agency. So the משנה is consistent: the 'be betrothed, be betrothed' clause is רבי שמעון, and the rule that only the father acts for a נערה is רבי יהודה's view, which רבי שמעון shares. The משנה therefore does not reflect the רבנן, so it does not refute ריש לקיש's explanation of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the old answer and gives a new one)
All of it, the whole משנה
Agency, appointing someone to act for you

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer for ריש לקיש: the משנה is רבי שמעון, who agrees with רבי יהודה that only the father acts for a נערה. So the משנה does not show what the רבנן hold, and ריש לקיש's claim about the רבנן still stands.

phrases.english: Rather: the whole of it is Rabbi Shimon,
and regarding agency he holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by reassigning the whole משנה to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattributing the author of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה, who agrees with רבי שמעון on oaths.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבי שמעון, who agrees with רבי יהודה on agency.

steps.title: Report from the study hall: everyone sided with רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי missed the study hall. רבי זירא tells him, through רבי אבין, that everyone sided with רבי יוחנן, and ריש לקיש shouted a פסוק that nobody listened to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי did not go to the study hall. He met רבי זירא and asked: What was said today in the study hall? He answered: I didn't go either. But רבי אבין went, and he said: The whole group sided with רבי יוחנן. And ריש לקיש cried out like a crane: 'And she departs... and she becomes,' but nobody paid attention to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש was received in the study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars sided with רבי יוחנן, who treats קידושין and גירושין differently for a נערה. ריש לקיש argued from the פסוק that joins divorce and marriage, so they should follow the same rules. Still, the study hall did not accept his view.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַסִּי לָא עָל לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi did not go into the study hall.
He found Rabbi Zeira,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי אֲמוּר הָאִידָּנָא בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא?
phrases.english: he said to him: What was said today in the study hall?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף אֲנָא לָא עֲיַילִ[י],
phrases.english: He said to him: I too did not go in,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected spelling, making it "I did not go in."

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin is the one who went in, and he said:
The entire group held like Rabbi Yochanan.
And Reish Lakish cried out like a crane:
"And she departs... and she becomes"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:2. Leaving one husband and becoming another's wife are placed side by side.

phrases.english: and there was no one who paid attention to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי לָא עָל לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending ריש לקיש to reporting how the study hall decided the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The study hall sided with רבי יוחנן against ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Is רבי אבין a reliable source?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי asks whether רבי אבין's report can be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is רבי אבין someone you can rely on?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי wants to know if this secondhand report is trustworthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report reached רבי אסי through two people, רבי אבין and then רבי זירא. Before treating it as the study hall's ruling, he checks that the source is solid.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone reliable, literally 'someone to lean on'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר סַמְכָא הוּא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is Rabbi Avin someone to rely on?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reliability of the report in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אבין's report is reliable.

steps.title: Yes, the report is fresh, like a fish from sea to pan
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says yes. The report is as fresh as a fish taken straight from the sea to the frying pan.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. It is like a fish going from the sea to the frying pan.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא confirms the report can be trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Very little time passed between the study hall session and רבי אבין's report. A fresh report has little chance of being garbled, so it is reliable.

keyTerms.meaning: Like from the sea to the frying pan, meaning very fresh

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
it is like from the sea to the frying pan.
phrases.notes: He means the report was brought right away, as fresh as a just-caught fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, כְּמִין יַמָּא לְטִיגְנֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The report is reliable because it was passed on right away.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes plain 'רבי אבין'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says he quotes this report in the name of 'רבי אבין' with no further detail, not a specific רבי אבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: I quote it not as רבי אבין son of רבי חייא, and not as רבי אבין בר כהנא, but simply as 'רבי אבין.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק clarifies exactly whose name this report is quoted in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were several אמוראים called רבי אבין. He will not pin the report on any specific one. He passes it on only as plain 'רבי אבין.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I quote it,
not as Rabbi Avin son of Rabbi Chiya,
and not as Rabbi Avin bar Kahana,
but as plain Rabbi Avin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the name of the source of the report in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The report is quoted in the name of an unspecified רבי אבין.

steps.title: Why does it matter which רבי אבין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the exact name makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we should care which רבי אבין said it. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the content is the same either way, the name seems unimportant. The גמרא wants a practical reason for רב נחמן בר יצחק's care.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the clarification in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference of naming a specific רבי אבין.

steps.title: It matters for contradictions between his own statements
steps.stepSummary: It matters when someone tries to show that a רבי אבין contradicts himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: To set his own statement against his own other statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the exact name matters when checking whether a rabbi contradicts himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If another ruling is quoted from a specific רבי אבין and seems to clash with this one, we can only call it a self-contradiction if both come from the same person. Since this report is from an unspecified רבי אבין, such a clash is not a real contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: His own statement against his own statement

steps.whatToRemember: The study hall sided with רבי יוחנן. The report is reliable, and it is quoted from an unspecified רבי אבין.

phrases.english: To raise a contradiction between his statement and his other statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exact name matters for deciding whether two rulings are a real self-contradiction.

steps.title: רבא asks רב נחמן a question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells us that רבא asked רב נחמן a question. This line sets up the question, which comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It tells us that רבא is about to ask רב נחמן something, and the actual question comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase בעא מיניה means a student or colleague is asking a real question, not attacking. It is not a קשיא. Here רבא turns to his teacher רב נחמן with a question, and the question itself comes after this line. This also marks a change of topic from the discussion about trusting רבי אבין's report.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him. This is the standard way the גמרא opens a sincere question to a teacher or colleague.
A leading אמורא in בבל who often discusses questions with his teacher רב נחמן.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבא (רָבָא, with a long 'a') with רבה (רַבָּה). They are two different אמוראים.

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Naḥman:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about whether רבי אבין's report can be trusted and opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question's content comes right after this line. This line only introduces רבא as the one asking and רב נחמן as the one being asked.
